subject: Cooking
title: Cilantro: Love It or Gene It
description: A fast breakdown of Cilantro: Love It or Gene It for builders.

hook.text: To some, cilantro tastes fresh and citrusy. To others, it tastes exactly like soap. Both are correct.

buildup.text: About 4–14% of the population has a genetic variant that makes cilantro taste soapy.

discovery.text: The gene OR6A2 detects aldehyde compounds in cilantro — the same chemicals found in soap.

twist.text: Crushing cilantro breaks down these aldehydes. Many 'haters' can tolerate it in pesto or chutney.

climax.text: Cilantro is essential to Mexican, Thai, Indian, and Chinese cuisines — billions love it, genes and all.

punchline.text: Whether cilantro tastes good is literally in your DNA.

quiz.question: What gene is linked to perceiving cilantro as soapy?

details.summary: Approximately 14 percent of people perceive cilantro as tasting like soap due to genetic variations in olfactory receptor genes, particularly OR6A2, that make them hypersensitive to aldehydes in the herb. For the rest, cilantro provides a bright, citrusy freshness essential to many global cuisines.
details.whyItMatters: Cilantro aversion is one of the clearest examples of genetic variation affecting food preference. It demonstrates that taste is partly biological, not just cultural.
takeaways: OR6A2 gene variants cause soap-like perception of cilantro
About 14 percent of people have this genetic sensitivity
Crushing cilantro breaks down the offending aldehyde compounds

faq.question: Can people who hate cilantro learn to like it?
faq.answer: Some people with the gene variant can develop tolerance through repeated exposure as the brain reclassifies the aldehyde signals. Crushing or cooking cilantro breaks down the soap-like aldehydes. However, those with strong genetic sensitivity may never enjoy fresh cilantro leaves.

faq.question: Are coriander seeds and cilantro from the same plant?
faq.answer: Yes. Cilantro is the leaf and stem while coriander is the dried seed. They taste completely different because the seed lacks the aldehydes that trigger the soap response. People who hate cilantro leaves often enjoy coriander seeds without any issue.
